name: Kerala
summary_text: Kerala was the first state in India to adopt a dedicated Policy for Transgenders, with named welfare measures including an overseas scholarship scheme administered through the Social Justice Department. A constituted welfare board exists. Kerala is one of only three states recording cases under the Transgender Persons Act in 2021 (2 of 7) and logged 4 of the 11 national cases in 2023, indicating the legal machinery is at least operational and that trans-targeted incidents are being formally registered rather than ignored. Against the national 0.43, Kerala sits +0.07. The policy infrastructure and scholarship scheme represent genuine state commitment to trans inclusion beyond the federal floor. Compared to Tamil Nadu (0.53), Kerala lacks the additional layer of active judicial endorsement (the Madras High Court commendation) and the longer institutional history since 1995, but its first-state policy status and operational board mark it clearly above the national norm. Compared to Assam (0.45), Kerala's protective framework is more developed and better documented. For a visitor, the practical benefit is institutional visibility: a trans-presenting person in Kochi or urban Kerala encounters a governance structure that has codified recognition, though like most Indian states, city-level norms in Thiruvananthapuram or Kochi are far more protective than rural areas.

sources.title: India’s crime data would have you believe that trans people barely face any violence—here’s why that doesn’t add up - Queerbeat
sources.claim_summary: queerbeat data report (30 Jan 2026): per the NCRB, the Transgender Persons Act recorded only 20 cases nationwide 2019-2023 - 1 in Tamil Nadu (2020); 7 in 2021 (2 each in Assam and Kerala, 3 in West Bengal); 1 in Tamil Nadu (2022); 11 in 2023 (7 Tamil Nadu, 4 Kerala), none from north and central India; it attributes the scarcity to police registration bias, against survey data showing 27.2% physical and 22.3% sexual violence prevalence (2025 Transgender Health study, n=4,964).

sources.title: Constitution of Transgender Welfare Boards/Commissions
sources.claim_summary: Press Information Bureau reply in the Rajya Sabha (8 Dec 2021, Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar): 12 states/UTs have constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under section 10(1) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 - Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chandigarh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
